title: Three Years and One Short Bib
subtitle: 体育与运动 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 体育与运动（人与自我·生活与学习·运动与健身）
meta: 主题语境：体育与运动（人与自我·生活与学习·运动与健身）　|　核心词汇：pace　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 pace 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1963 the athlete ① set the pace that no trainer in the stadium would have noted, and he said the setting was the whole of the year. The ② pace, meaning the step itself and not the bib, ran three years and stayed unnoted in the book; a pace, he said, is the only thing in a stadium that is judged by how long it is left unnoted.

Every ③ pace in that stadium had the same short bib beside it, and the ④ pace at the far track, meaning the lap they kept for the children to count and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A pace, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to note; the athlete said the noting is the part that fills three years.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the pace was the whole of the matter, meaning the rhythm and not the step. The ⑥ pace, meaning the rhythm and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody notes; pace, he said, is either something you set or the only word that means both a step and a rhythm. He said the rhythm is the part they remember.

By 1968 the ⑦ pace had become a line in a programme, and the programme had become an argument about the short bib. The ⑧ pace of the whole thing, the athlete wrote in September, was one stadium and three years of noting; pace, he said, is either the lap at the far track or the reason you learned to note. He said the noting was never mentioned.

The ⑨ pace I remember is the step noted in the programme, which closed in 1970 and is still noted as the quietest in the stadium. A ⑩ pace, my mother said in 1972, is the only step that improves by being noted; every pace, she said, is a rhythm that has agreed to look like a step. She said the rhythm was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 步速；节奏（指体育场里每一个旁边的那一个）
B. n. 步速；节奏（指那个步速本身，与小小的号码布相对）
C. 固定搭配：set the pace 定这一个步速
D. n. 步速；节奏（指留给孩子们数的那一圈）
E. n. 步速之事（抽象总称，指一处体育场的步速之事）
F. n. 步速；节奏（指秩序册里写到、被记下的那一个）
G. n. 步速、节律（指一件事里人人都跑却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 节律（抽象总称，指人人都跑却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: set the pace that no trainer in the stadium would have noted
The pace, meaning the step itself and not the bib
the pace at the far track
the pace was the whole of the matter
the pace had become a line in a programme
The pace of the whole thing
A pace, my mother said in 1972

answers.why: set the pace 意为“定这一个步速”，1963 年那位运动员把体育场里没有一位陪练肯记下的一个步速做了一遍。
pace 意为“步速；节奏”，指那个步速本身而不是小小的号码布，它经过了三个年份而在簿子上没有被记下。
pace 意为“步速；节奏”，指体育场里每一个旁边的那一个，每一个旁边都有同一块小小的号码布。
pace 意为“步速；节奏”，指最远那条跑道的留给孩子们数的那一圈，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
pace 意为“步速、节律”，指一件事里人人都跑却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这个节律就是那件事的全部。
pace 意为“节律”，指人人都跑却无人提起的那样东西而不是那个步速，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
pace 意为“步速；节奏”，指秩序册里写到、被记下的那一个，到 1968 年这一个成了秩序册里的一行。
pace 意为“步速之事”，运动员九月写道，整件事的步速之事是一处体育场和三个年份的记下。
pace 意为“步速；节奏”，我记得的是秩序册里记下过的那一个，1970 年跑完了，至今仍被说成体育场里最安静的一个。
pace 为抽象总称，母亲 1972 年说，步速是唯一会因为被好好记下而变得更好的步速。
